content.thinking: This looks like a classic memory leak pattern: memory climbing from ~460MB to 1.38GB while traffic stays flat at 1200 and there's no process restart, with latency degrading as a result. No deployments in the past 7 days, and the issue began around 23:14-23:18 with memory starting to rise.

hypotheses.subject: io-shop heap (memory_used_bytes)
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's heap climbs monotonically from ~460MB to ~1.38GB starting around 23:14-23:18 while request volume stays flat at 1200/min and the process is never restarted; latency (p50 45→147ms, p99 ~375→1231ms) degrades as the heap grows, consistent with GC pressure from an unreleased allocation. No deploy, config change or flag toggle is recorded in the preceding week, and error rate stays at baseline, ruling out an upstream failure.

supporting_evidence.claim: memory_used_bytes climbs steadily with flat traffic: 2026-09-22T23:14:00Z 477302585 → 23:18:00Z 612678329 → 23:30:00Z 969563659 → 23:43:00Z 1381396700, request_volume constant at 1200
process_start_time_seconds unchanged at 1790077411.885196 across the whole span — same process, no restart, so the growth accumulates with uptime
WARN io-shop: heap at 1024MiB of 2048MiB limit ... heap at 1324MiB of 2048MiB limit
Latency degrades in lockstep with heap: p50 45→147ms, p95 219→719ms, p99 368→1231ms from 23:33 to 23:43 while volume is unchanged
Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-15T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-22T23:43:31Z. (nothing changed in this window)

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: a latent code path shipped earlier (outside the 7-day change window) began leaking under a particular request mix. The evidence would look identical, but no deployment is visible in any window read, so this is unsupported by retrieved evidence.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-21T23:18:00Z to 2026-09-22T23:18:00Z. (nothing changed in this window)

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: the ongoing low-level 'ClientDisconnected' errors on the account page represent clients abandoning slow requests, and some external pressure is the true driver. The errors are however at baseline rate throughout (0.5-3%, the same as hours before onset) and no dependency is named in the logs, so this does not explain the memory climb.

supporting_evidence.claim: ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection (present continuously from 22:48, well before onset, at unchanged rate)
